reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses deformation twins in Al alloys and CoCrFeMnNi, not thermally induced twins in FeMnCoCrNi. E2 addresses magnetic homogeneity from Pd additions and annealing in NiFeCoCrPd, not twin boundaries. E3 describes a deformation-induced twin network in CrCoNi for mechanical properties, with no link to magnetic or magnetocaloric behavior. None of the evidence connects twin boundaries to modified magnetic exchange, steep magnetization change, or enhanced heat exchange.
premises: Nanoscale twin boundaries can be induced in FeMnCoCrNi by heat treatment near the order–disorder transition.
Twin boundaries locally modify magnetic exchange interactions and magnetostructural coupling.
Modified exchange/coupling enables a steep magnetization change at low applied fields.
Twin boundaries facilitate rapid heat exchange and reduce hysteresis.
The engineered twin network preserves mechanical stability.
